name: FRED and ALFRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)
provider: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
rate_limits: 120 requests per minute, then HTTP 429 (source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/errors.html). The public CSV download link needs no key and has no published limit.
history_start: Varies by series. Fed H.10 FX from 1971 (EUR from 1999), WTI from 1986, VIX from 1990, OECD 3-month rates vary by country.
what_it_has: Hundreds of thousands of US and international series: exchange rates, interest rates, inflation, jobs, oil and gas prices, and the VIX. ALFRED keeps every past version of a series, so you can see what a number looked like on the day it came out.
simple: A giant free library of economic numbers run by a US central bank office. It is where we get our currency prices, interest rates and oil prices.
license_terms: Free to use under the FRED API terms. Apps must say they use the FRED API and are not endorsed by the St. Louis Fed. Some series belong to other owners (for example S&P and CBOE) and are marked Copyright; personal use is fine but other use needs the owner's permission. https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/terms_of_use.html
quality_notes: H.10 FX rates are noon New York buying rates, not closing prices. The OECD interbank rates for the euro area and UK currently stop at 2026-01. SP500 only covers the last 10 years and has no dividends.

relevance.reason: Our main source for FX, rates and commodity prices, and the only free one with first release values.
